explanation: Tipping (Trinkgeld) in Germany is a polite way to reward good service but is never mandatory, since staff earn a regular wage and service is already built into menu prices. Most diners round the bill up or add roughly 5-10%, handing the cash directly to the server rather than leaving it on the table.
local_tip: When paying in cash, round up or add about 10% and tell the server the total you want to pay while saying 'Stimmt so' ('keep the change').

also_check.note: Tipping is considered unnecessary and can even seem insulting, since excellent service is already the baseline expectation.
Tipping 15-20% is the norm and socially expected, since many servers rely on tips to make up a large share of their income.
A service charge is included by law, but rounding up or leaving small change for good service is still a common courtesy.
